nodes.description: Biallelic frameshift, splice and exon-deletion variants remove or truncate M1AP. The only molecular activity demonstrated for M1AP is binding to the ZZS proteins SHOC1, TEX11 and SPO16, shown by co-immunoprecipitation for the mouse and the human proteins. Truncated M1AP proteins modelled on patient alleles no longer bind TEX11, so the disease alleles abolish the one activity the protein is known to have.

nodes.description: Most spermatocytes progress through prophase I and arrest at metaphase I with misaligned chromosomes, then undergo apoptosis. The arrest is partial: some metaphase cells align correctly, escape apoptosis, and complete meiosis, so round and occasionally elongated spermatids are found. This partial metaphase I arrest differs from the early zygotene to pachytene arrest caused by loss of SHOC1, TEX11 or SPO16.

nodes.description: Early recombination proceeds: double-strand breaks form and are repaired, and homologous chromosomes synapse fully. What is reduced is the number of MSH5-marked recombination intermediates and of MLH1-marked class I crossovers. In the one human case quantified, MSH5 foci fell to about half and MLH1 foci to about 35 against 48 per spermatocyte, although every homologue pair still carried at least one crossover in the cell examined.

nodes.description: M1AP localises to the chromosome axes of spermatocytes in a SPO16-dependent manner and colocalises with TEX11. Its loss leaves SHOC1 in place but reduces the TEX11 recruited to recombination intermediates, by about two thirds in the one human spermatocyte spread analysed. The ZZS complex is not abolished, which distinguishes this lesion from loss of SHOC1, TEX11 or SPO16 themselves, where TEX11 foci are absent.
